summary: Signal complete ordered membership state when held windows do not change

replay.detail: Exposes existing indexed live counts and the maximum of the container changed index and local repair watermark. No projection authority, replay order, shared digest, checkpoint witness or retention rule changes.

schema.detail: No database tables, indexes, meta keys, numeric schema version or shared projection layout changes. Membership state is read from existing transactional projections.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules remain version 14. Host-local invalidation frontiers remain excluded from shared projection digests and checkpoint answers.

compatibility.detail: Ordered-memberships snapshot and changes frames now require membership {container, live_count, changed_index}. Generated Rust, TypeScript and Swift clients expose this state and require it when decoding membership data frames. Resource frames remain unchanged. Upgrade these draft clients and server together; cross-version clients have not been exercised. Capability versions and pairing scopes are unchanged.

downtime.detail: No startup migration, replay or additional background work is introduced. The count and frontier are read in the same snapshot as the held rows, with no lifetime-history scan.

manual.detail: No new manual data migration is required. Consumers use the opaque monotonic changed_index only within one snapshot.host_id to invalidate complete-set reads. Canonical-winner-preserving v1 placement migration and exclusive reader/writer cutover remain in the follow-up stacked PR above #1958.

recovery.detail: No recovery procedure changes. The exposed frontier has no cross-host ordering or canonical revision meaning and is not checkpoint authority; previous backup and roll-forward guidance remains applicable.
